response: ## Accessibility Issue: Field Hint Insufficient Color Contrast **Bug ID:** `A11Y-f8a2c9d1` (instance) / `A11X-b3e7f4a0` (pattern) **URL:** https://app.example.io/settings/profile **XPath:** `//span[@class='field-hint' and contains(text(), 'Shown on your public profile')]` **Full DOM path:** `/html/body/main/section[@id='settings']/div[@id='display-name-field']/following-sibling::span[@class='field-hint']` *(reconstructed from CSS target; full ancestor chain unavailable in raw scan output)* **WCAG SC:** 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) (Level AA) **Rule:** axe-core 4.9.1 — `color-contrast` **Severity:** High **Frequency:** 1 instance on this page **Screen type:** desktop | **Colour mode:** light ### HTML Snippet ```html Shown on your public profile ``` ### Description The field hint text uses a foreground color (`#8b8b8b`) against a background of `#f5f5f5`, resulting in a contrast ratio of 3.13:1. This falls below the WCAG AA minimum threshold of 4.5:1 for normal-sized text (14px). The secondary hint "Optional" on the pronouns field exhibits the identical issue. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Navigate to https://app.example.io/settings/profile 2. Locate the "Display Name" and "Pronouns" input fields 3. Observe the helper text beneath each field (e.g., "Shown on your public profile") 4. Measure contrast using a browser accessibility inspector or manual color picker ### Expected Behaviour Helper text should meet WCAG AA minimum contrast ratio of 4.5:1 against its background. ### Actual Behaviour Helper text has a contrast ratio of 3.13:1, failing WCAG AA requirements. ### Testing Environment | Item | Value | |---|---| | Browser | Chrome 126 on Windows 11 | | OS | Windows 11 | | Screen reader | N/A (automated scan) | | Testing tool | axe-core 4.9.1 | ### Impact Users with low vision, color blindness, or those using high-contrast modes may struggle to read the helper text, leading to confusion about what information will be publicly visible. The issue degrades readability but does not block core functionality. ### Suggested Fix (optional) Increase the contrast of the hint text. For example, change `color: #8b8b8b` to `#595959` or darker, ensuring a minimum 4.5:1 ratio against `#f5f5f5`. ```css .field-hint { color: #595959; /* or darker */ } ``` --- ## Accessibility Issue: Help Icon Link Missing Accessible Name **Bug ID:** `A11Y-c4d8e2f3` (instance) / `A11X-a1b2c3d4` (pattern) **URL:** https://app.example.io/settings/profile **XPath:** `//a[@class='help-icon']` **Full DOM path:** `/html/body/main/section[@id='visibility-section']/a[@class='help-icon']` *(reconstructed from CSS target; full ancestor chain unavailable in raw scan output)* **WCAG SC:** 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (Level A) **Rule:** axe-core 4.9.1 — `link-name` **Severity:** Critical **Frequency:** 1 instance on this page **Screen type:** desktop | **Colour mode:** light ### HTML Snippet ```html ``` ### Description The help icon link contains only a decorative SVG with `aria-hidden="true"` and no visible text, `aria-label`, or `title` attribute. Screen reader users and voice control software cannot determine the purpose of this interactive element. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Navigate to https://app.example.io/settings/profile 2. Open a screen reader (e.g., NVDA, VoiceOver) or enable voice control 3. Navigate to the "Visibility" section and move focus to the help icon link 4. Listen to what the assistive technology announces ### Expected Behaviour Screen readers should announce a meaningful label such as "Help with profile visibility" or equivalent, allowing users to understand the link's purpose. ### Actual Behaviour Assistive technologies announce only "link" with no accessible name, making it impossible for screen reader and voice control users to identify its function. ### Testing Environment | Item | Value | |---|---| | Browser | Chrome 126 on Windows 11 | | OS | Windows 11 | | Screen reader | NVDA 2024.1 / VoiceOver (simulated) | | Testing tool | axe-core 4.9.1 | ### Impact Blind and low-vision users relying on screen readers cannot identify or activate the help link. Users who rely on voice control software cannot trigger the link by speaking its label. This blocks access to critical guidance for managing profile visibility settings, constituting a core task barrier. ### Suggested Fix (optional) Add an `aria-label` to the anchor element or include visually hidden text: ```html Help with profile visibility ```
